player-open.question: Is your player open on this PC?
player-open.help: Lyrica follows the Windows media session, so the player must be running locally.

open-player.title: Open the player first
open-player.fix: Start Spotify, Apple Music or Cider on the same PC, then play a track. A phone casting to a speaker is not a Windows media session.
steps: Open the desktop player, not the mobile app.
Play one track for at least ten seconds.
Open the Windows media flyout and confirm the track is listed.

playing.question: Is it actually playing?
playing.help: A paused track can still appear in the media flyout, but Lyrica will show a paused state.

start-playback.title: Start playback
start-playback.fix: Press play in the player. If the player says it is playing but Windows shows it as paused, restart the player's media session by pausing and resuming once.
steps: Press play in the desktop app.
Check the Windows media flyout shows the same status.
If it is stale, close and reopen the player.

lyrics-found.question: Does the status panel say a timed lyric was found?
lyrics-found.help: Open the status panel from the tray. It checks the player, the track and the lyric provider separately.

no-lyrics.title: No timed lyric found
no-lyrics.fix: The track may be missing from the provider, or the title and artist may not match. Play a well-known track to test, then try the other provider in Settings. If the song is instrumental or unreleased, there may be no timed lyric yet.
steps: Try a different, popular track.
Open Settings and change the lyric provider order.
Check the status panel for the exact title and artist Lyrica received.
If the title is wrong, the player is reporting bad metadata.

timing.question: Are the words early, late or in time?
timing.help: Use the nudge control. The offset lasts for that song and resets on the next track.

offset-early.title: Words arrive early
offset-early.fix: Nudge the lyrics later with the +1s control until the highlight lands on the vocal. If the whole song is consistently off, the provider's timing was authored against a different master.
steps: Use the on-screen nudge control.
Adjust in one-second steps, then smaller if needed.
Keep the same track while you adjust so the offset applies to this song.

offset-late.title: Words arrive late
offset-late.fix: Nudge the lyrics earlier with the −1s control. If the first line is late but later lines drift further, the timing source is the problem, not a constant offset.
steps: Use the −1s nudge control.
Check whether the drift gets worse across the song.
If it drifts, try another lyric provider.

overlay.question: Is the overlay missing over a game?
overlay.help: Exclusive fullscreen bypasses the desktop compositor.

fullscreen.title: Switch the game to borderless
fullscreen.fix: Exclusive fullscreen bypasses the desktop compositor, so Lyrica steps aside instead of drawing over the game. Set the game to borderless windowed and the overlay can return.
steps: Open the game's display settings.
Choose Borderless or Windowed Fullscreen.
Bring Lyrica's overlay back from the tray.

contact.title: Still stuck?
contact.fix: Copy diagnostics from the status panel, then send it with your Windows version, player and the track that failed. The screenshot and the four status rows are usually enough to find the problem.
steps: Open the status panel.
Choose Copy diagnostics.
Email support or ask in the Discord troubleshooting channel.
